I believe health prevention is crucial to keeping healthcare costs down in Switzerland.
I think focusing on prevention feels like the state is meddling too much in my personal life.
I feel that early health education in schools can create a healthier society for everyone.
I’m convinced that prevention efforts are a waste of money since many people won’t change their habits.
I strongly support more national campaigns to raise awareness about healthy living.
I’m annoyed by the idea of more health campaigns
column2: they just clutter my life with unnecessary messages.

column1: I think it’s vital to invest more in prevention to avoid expensive treatments later.
I believe spending on prevention is pointless when we already struggle to treat existing illnesses.
I feel that a healthier environment, like more green spaces, would naturally improve our health.
I’m skeptical that changing environments for health reasons justifies the huge costs involved.
I’m convinced that teaching health skills from a young age can prevent many diseases.
I think forcing health education on kids is overstepping
I support stricter rules on advertising unhealthy products like alcohol and tobacco.
I’m against banning ads for alcohol and tobacco; it’s my choice what I consume, not the state’s.
I believe higher taxes on unhealthy products can push people to make better choices.
I’m frustrated by higher taxes on things like sugar
column2: it just makes life harder for poorer people.

column1: I think prevention is a shared responsibility between individuals and society.
I feel that prevention is entirely up to me
column2: the government shouldn’t interfere at all.

column1: I’m glad that focusing on prevention could reduce the burden on our healthcare system.
I’m worried that too much focus on prevention distracts from urgent care for sick people now.
I believe that national coordination of prevention efforts would make them more effective.
I’m against national health prevention laws
column2: they ignore local needs and differences in Switzerland.

column1: I think vulnerable groups need special prevention programs to stay healthy.
I feel that targeting specific groups for prevention is unfair and creates division.
I’m convinced that prevention can improve my quality of life in the long run.
